transcript:
MEETING HEADER:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (Norfield - Head of ML), Owen Li (Norfield - Platform), Samir Patel (Norfield - CISO), Leah Thompson (Norfield - Product), Ben Carroll (Norfield - SRE)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style readout focusing on recent cost spike around inference, reliability anomalies on peak windows, and a handoff to security for private deployment discussion. Agreement to run a dedicated benchmark and deliver security artifacts. Several clarifications on network egress and KMS/HSM expectations.

Topics Covered:
- Cost variance on month-to-date usage and tail latency impact
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs for Norfield workloads
- SLOs: 95th vs 99th latency, p99 token generation for chat flows
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs retention
- Pilot next steps: pricing, perf benchmark, deployment checklist

TIMESTAMPED TRANSCRIPT BODY:
[00:00] Alex Chen: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:05] Marta Ruiz: Marta here, hi.
[00:07] Owen Li: Owen - platform.
[00:09] Samir Patel: Samir - security.
[00:11] Leah Thompson: Leah - product.
[00:13] Ben Carroll: Ben - SRE.
[00:15] Alex Chen: cool, I'll kick off with a 2min summary of what we saw last month; Priya will cover the perf notes and then we'll hand to Samir for security items.
[00:28] Priya Nair: thanks Alex; so the salient point is the cost bump that happened mid-May - you folks saw about a 38% uplift month-over-month which correlates with longer token streams on your conversational assistant. We looked at batching profiles and there was less effective batching because many requests hit small-LLM fallbacks — or sorry small prefix caches — oh man the auto transcript does fun things, but basically KV cache wasn't being leveraged as much as expected.
[01:03] Ben Carroll: yeah we changed the frontend to stream earlier which reduced client-side latency but increased overall token count, and some warm-up patterns created short bursts.
[01:18] Priya Nair: exactly, that pattern increases per-token cost and also pushes different kernel paths so your GPU occupancy suffers at small sequence sizes. We recommended two levers: increase prefix caching and nudge the client to batch micro-requests when feasible.
[01:37] Owen Li: when you say prefix caching do you mean Redwood's prefix cache or our app-level caching?
[01:42] Priya Nair: good q — we mean both. Redwood can do automatic prefix/KV caching at the runtime and you can also coalesce requests at the edge. There's a config we can suggest for your edge router + SDK.
[01:56] Marta Ruiz: ok, what about model choice — we tried switching to a smaller quantized model during peak windows to save cost but saw worse latency p99.
[02:07] Priya Nair: that's the tradeoff — quantized smaller variants reduce compute cost but some models have higher decode latency for long sequences; also fallbacks can cause throughput cliffs. For your long chat sessions we suggested a hybrid routing policy: keep a high-capacity variant for sessions predicted to exceed X tokens and route short replies to the quantized variant.
[02:30] Alex Chen: Marta, you previously said success criteria were <200ms p95 and p99 under 600ms for user-visible steps?
[02:39] Marta Ruiz: correct, those are product goals, though we can tolerate occasional p99 spikes if overall UX is good.
[02:47] Samir Patel: from security taxonomy, the main asks are: SOC2 artifacts, SSO via SAML, audit logs for model inputs+outputs for 90 days, and KMS integration for key management. We also need clarity on data residency — some customers of ours require EU-only data at rest.
[03:10] Alex Chen: noted. Priya, can Redwood's private deployment meet those?
[03:14] Priya Nair: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages, KMS integration with customer-managed keys and HSM is possible; the audit logs are generated by the control plane. We will send the SOC2 pack and the KMS integration doc after the call.
[03:29] Leah Thompson: are there extra costs for Private?
[03:32] Alex Chen: yes typically Private is an enterprise license plus infra; Dedicated reserved capacity can be a middle ground with predictable throughput and lower unit costs than hosted at scale. We'll share a pricing comparison.
[03:45] Ben Carroll: we need to know network egress rules; if we run Private in our VPC do you require open outbound to Redwood control plane?
[03:54] Priya Nair: for VPC mode there's an option for a customer-managed control plane tunnel or a limited egress policy; we can push the control plane endpoints into your peered subnet in some setups. We'll include a matrix in the checklist.
[04:08] Owen Li: on the perf side, can we run a dedicated benchmark with representative traffic? We want to reproduce the p99 spike.
[04:13] Priya Nair: absolutely — recommend a 90-minute test during a quiet window, we'll instrument tracing and token-level cost. Ben can also bring his 48h traffic sample.
[04:25] Marta Ruiz: timeline wise we need to present to finance by July 8th. So if we can get pricing and a benchmark result by end of month that helps.
[04:34] Alex Chen: that's doable. We'll aim to deliver pricing and start bench week of 6/29, deliver initial results by 7/2.
[04:42] Samir Patel: one note — for audit logs we need immutability and chain-of-custody metadata. Is Redwood able to sign logs or ship them to our SIEM with integrity checks?
[04:54] Priya Nair: Redwood can stream audit logs to your S3 or SIEM and we support log signing with a key; we'll confirm the exact integrity guarantees in the SOC2 pack.
[05:05] Leah Thompson: any blockers from Redwood's side for a pilot?
[05:08] Alex Chen: no blockers; we need your 48h traffic sample and a PO or pilot acceptance criteria doc. We'll supply the pilot pricing scenarios.
[05:16] Jordan Alvarez: as CSM I'll coordinate the timeline and make sure we hit the finance deadline.
[05:21] Ben Carroll: quick question on throttles and graceful degradation — we saw some 500s during the spike. Can Redwood fall back to a smaller model automatically?
[05:31] Priya Nair: yes, we have routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; plus canary rollout and circuit-breaker settings. We can propose default fallback thresholds.
[05:42] Marta Ruiz: good. Also curious what bench metrics you recommend — besides p95/p99 and tokens per second?
[05:48] Priya Nair: we'd collect latency percentiles, GPU occupancy, kernel selection logs, effective batching rate, and token-cost breakdown. Also trace the prefix cache hit rate.
[05:59] Owen Li: if we do Dedicated reserved capacity how much lead time to spin up capacity in our region?
[06:04] Alex Chen: depends on region and demand, typically 2-4 weeks for reserved pools to be provisioned and warmed, less if we have available capacity.
[06:12] Samir Patel: about compliance — we need to ensure redaction capabilities for PII before logs leave our environment. Is there a redact-before-export option?
[06:20] Priya Nair: yes, we can configure input/output filtering and redact at runtime; this is part of the private deployment checklist variations.
[06:28] Marta Ruiz: ok sounds good.
[06:30] [10:00] (interlude — demo link shared: Redwood pilot pricing doc)
[16:05] Alex Chen: jumping ahead to next steps — recap: we'll share pricing, SOC2 pack, VPC checklist, and schedule perf benchmark.
[16:15] Ben Carroll: Ben will send the traffic sample and proposed perf window.
[16:20] Samir Patel: I'll validate KMS/HSM and provide a short list of constraints.
[16:25] Leah Thompson: product wants a short evaluation plan template to sign off on pilot success.
[16:30] Alex Chen: Jordan will share an evaluation plan template; Alex will send pricing. Priya sends VPC and SOC docs.
[16:40] Marta Ruiz: thanks — I also want the model routing config example so our engineers can test locally.
[16:45] Priya Nair: will include a sample routing JSON and suggested SDK knobs.
[16:50] Owen Li: last question — if we hit capacity limits on hosted during peak, do you auto-burst to Dedicated or do we need to pre-provision?
[16:58] Alex Chen: we support policy-based routing; we can set up fallback to compatible capacity tiers and regions, but burst behavior to Dedicated typically requires pre-arranged reserved capacity or a contractual burst ordering — we can discuss flexible burst add-ons.
[17:12] Samir Patel: ok thanks everyone.
[17:15] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts.

Action Items (in-call):
- Alex: Pricing scenarios doc (due 2026-06-21).
- Priya: VPC & SOC2 docs, KMS integration pattern (due 2026-06-20).
- Ben Carroll: 48h traffic sample + preferred bench window (due 2026-06-25).
- Samir Patel: security constraints list including HSM needs (due 2026-06-24).

Questions Raised:
- Can Redwood redact PII before logs export? (answered: yes, config available)
- What are the latency tradeoffs with quantized vs non-quantized variants? (discussed: sometimes higher decode latency for quantized long sequences)
- Does Dedicated provisioning have lead time? (discussed: typically 2-4 weeks)

References Shared:
- Link: Pilot pricing spreadsheet (shared by Alex)
- Link: VPC & SOC2 checklist (to be shared by Priya)
- Link: Sample routing JSON (to be included in follow-up)

END OF TRANSCRIPT
